data.generation: Euler-Maruyama at dt = 0.001 for the circadian ground truth (see ground_truth_sde). Observations are every 0.05 on [0, 4] (81 points per trajectory). The paper's circadian training sets use 50 trajectories per (sigma0, c) combination; the horizon printed in the PMC text is t in [0, 1], but a [0, 1] window covers only 0.21 rad of the oscillator (period 2*pi/beta ~= 29.9), so the horizon is extended here to T = 4 (0.84 rad, damping factor exp(-0.76) ~= 0.47) as a declared deviation, to include a visible damped-oscillation arc.
data.initial_law: x_0 = 0, y_0 = 1 for every trajectory (paper Section 3.1: initial condition (x(0), y(0)) = (0, 1))

distillation.diffusion_targets: Cholesky entries (L11, L21, L22, L12) of the teacher diffusion matrix, with L12 fixed to 0 by the triangular identification (same convention as Day 4). Headline diffusion error is the joint NRMSE over all four entries; per-entry RMS errors and the implied covariance Sigma = L L^T NRMSE are reported separately because the W2/marginal training objective identifies the distribution, hence Sigma, not L itself.
distillation.library_variables: polynomials in (x, y) only, where x = per mRNA concentration and y = per protein concentration (dimensionless). The system is time-homogeneous; no t variable in the library.
distillation.oracle_diagnostic: the same SINDy procedure fitted to ground-truth field values at the same query states (diagnostic ceiling only, not a candidate)
distillation.query_states: observed states of each split (trajectory-disjoint train/validation/test), teacher evaluated directly (no finite differences)
distillation.selection: per field, minimize validation NRMSE against the teacher; test evaluated once after selection

ground_truth_sde.form: d x_t = (-alpha x_t - beta y_t) dt + sigma0 dB1_t + sigma0 c dB2_t; d y_t = (beta x_t - alpha y_t) dt + sigma0 c dB1_t + sigma0 dB2_t. Equivalently the diffusion matrix is the constant L = sigma0 [[1, c], [c, 1]], so Sigma = L L^T = sigma0^2 [[1 + c^2, 2c], [2c, 1 + c^2]]. x = per mRNA, y = per protein (dimensionless).
ground_truth_sde.note: Paper Eq. (9) with alpha = 0.19, beta = 0.21 (paper Section 3.1) and the constant-diffusion form Eq. (11) at one slice (sigma0, c) = (0.20, 0.50) of the paper's 25-combination grid (sigma0 in 0.10..0.30, c in 0.2..1.0). The paper's END-nSDE takes (x, y, sigma0, c) as inputs and reconstructs a family of SDEs; here a single slice is cut and the teacher does NOT take (sigma0, c) as inputs (declared cut, see teacher deviation). The Langevin and linear diffusion forms (Eqs. 12-13) are not treated today.

H2_diffusion_distillation.note: Headline is the Cholesky-entry joint NRMSE; the Sigma clause is the identified-object clause. Both must hold.

H3_truth_recovery.note: Field clause plus a linear-coefficient clause: the truth drift is linear, so the symbolic drift's expanded constant + linear coefficients are compared with (constant 0, linear matrix [[-alpha, -beta], [beta, -alpha]]) by RMSE over the 6 entries (2 constants + 4 linear coefficients). The threshold is loosened relative to the paper's reported mean drift error 0.15 for the constant-diffusion case because (i) this teacher is a single-slice cut trained by an approximated (marginal + covariance) W2 objective, not the paper's full joint W2 training, and (ii) the teacher is a generic MLP, not the paper's parameter-conditioned network. A coefficient clause is included only together with the pre-fit collinearity gate (Day 1 reflection).

H4_simulation.domain_excursion_definition: fraction of simulated trajectories whose radius sqrt(x^2 + y^2) ever exceeds 2.0 (twice the initial radius 1.0) at any simulated step; a domain-validity measure separate from failure (Day 4 reflection).
H4_simulation.note: Paired RMSE is in (x, y) coordinates; the threshold is set from the terminal scale (state std ~0.5-0.7). Failure radius is 5.0 (5x the initial radius); radius excursions above 2.0 are counted as domain excursions, not failures, unless the trajectory is non-finite or exceeds radius 5.0.

H5_estimator_comparison_w2_vs_em.note: Verdict clauses: (a) the W2 teacher's test temporally-decoupled marginal-W2 loss (mean over observation times of the per-dimension sorted-marginal squared W2 distance plus the covariance-mismatch term, same definition as the W2 training loss) is smaller than the EM teacher's on the same test trajectories simulated from the same initial condition; (b) the W2 teacher's Sigma NRMSE vs truth (test query states) is no worse than the EM teacher's by more than the tie zone 0.01 (Day 3 reflection: a within-zone difference is a tie, and the verdict then rests on clause (a)). Drift NRMSE ordering alone does NOT decide the verdict (Day 4 reflection: drift is weakly identified at dt_obs = 0.05, so drift absolute RMS errors and Sigma errors are reported alongside). Clause (a) is biased in favour of the W2 teacher because the metric is its training objective; this bias is declared here and the clause is read as a paper-axis check, not as a neutral estimator ranking.

H6_paper_axis_downstream.note: Paper-axis proxy, NOT the paper's reconstruction-error claim: the paper reports mean drift error 0.15 and mean diffusion error 0.16 for the constant-diffusion case over its 25-combination grid. Here the downstream proxy is the terminal-time (t = 4) mean radius E[sqrt(x^2 + y^2)] of simulated trajectories: |radius_symbolic - radius_teacher| <= 0.05, with the paired standard error reported. If the paired SE is comparable to the threshold (SE >= 0.025), the clause is reported as 'not statistically established' even if the point estimate passes (Day 4 reflection). Paired simulation uses common Brownian increments.

paper.authors: Jiancheng Zhang, Xiangting Li, Xiaolu Guo, Zhaoyi You, Lucas Bottcher, Alex Mogilner, Alexander Hoffmann, Tom Chou, Mingtao Xia
paper.experiment: Section 3.1: circadian clock model Eq. (9) with alpha = 0.19, beta = 0.21, initial (0, 1); three diffusion forms (constant Eq. 11, Langevin Eq. 12, linear Eq. 13); 25 combinations of (sigma0, c); 50 trajectories per combination; END-nSDE trained by temporally-decoupled squared W2 loss, taking state and (sigma0, c) as inputs
paper.title: Reconstructing noisy gene regulation dynamics using extrinsic-noise-driven neural stochastic differential equations

reflections_applied.day1_collinearity_gate: Train-query corr(x, y), VIF and degree-2 feature correlations are computed before fitting; the coefficient clause in H3 is read only together with this gate. The Day 1 discretization-bias diagnostic is adapted: EM vs W2 teachers are compared on drift and Sigma field errors, split by regime (radius < 0.5 vs >= 0.5, and early t < 1 vs late t >= 2), and the distilled teacher is fixed a priori to the W2 teacher because the paper's method is W2-based and distribution matching is the paper-axis question.
reflections_applied.day1_discretization_bias: See day1_collinearity_gate: the two estimators compared are EM transition likelihood (freezing f and Sigma over dt_obs = 0.05) and the W2 simulation-based estimator (no freezing; teacher simulated at dt_sim = 0.01). The diagnostic question is whether freezing over the observation interval biases the constant-diffusion level.
reflections_applied.day2_nll_sensitivity: Estimator ordering is judged by field NRMSE and by the W2 distribution metric, never by transition NLL alone; NLL is reported only as a diagnostic for the EM teacher.
reflections_applied.day2_off_manifold: Off-manifold grid diagnosis is standard: (x, y) in {-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1} x {-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1} (25 points), reported on field / coefficient / off-manifold axes separately. The grid overlaps the marginal data range, so it is not claimed as strong extrapolation (Day 3 reflection); its diagnostic power is deviation from the joint (spiral-band) distribution.
reflections_applied.day3_common_random_numbers: Paired simulation and the terminal-radius downstream metric (H6) use common Brownian increments across models, so model differences are not confounded with independent Monte Carlo error.
reflections_applied.day3_diffusion_tie_zone: The Sigma comparison in H5 carries a pre-declared tie zone of 0.01 in Sigma NRMSE; a within-zone difference is a tie, and the H5 verdict then rests on the W2-loss clause.
reflections_applied.day4_domain_validity: H4 carries a domain-excursion clause (radius > 2.0 rate) separate from the failure rate: a model with failure rate 0 but a high excursion rate is not read as 'pass' on domain validity.
reflections_applied.day4_downstream_paired_se: H6 reports the paired standard error of the terminal-radius difference alongside the point estimate, and marks the clause indeterminate if the paired SE is comparable to the threshold.
reflections_applied.day4_high_order_cancellation: Large high-degree symbolic coefficients are read as manifold-cancellation / off-manifold blow-up risk, not as physical meaning, and are checked against the off-manifold grid.
reflections_applied.day4_weak_drift_identification: Drift comparisons report absolute RMS errors and Sigma errors alongside NRMSE, and note denominator effects where the truth drift field is small (near the origin, where both drift components approach 0).

simulation.initial_states: test trajectories' states at t=0 (all (0, 1) by construction)

teacher.architecture: Generic MLP neural SDE in the paper's spirit (feed-forward networks for drift and diffusion): drift MLP (x, y) -> R^2, hidden [32, 32] tanh; diffusion MLP (x, y) -> (L11, L21, L22) with L11 = softplus(raw) + 0.01, L22 = softplus(raw) + 0.01, L21 unconstrained, L12 = 0 fixed. The triangular form fixes the orthogonal rotation ambiguity: the distribution identifies Sigma = L L^T, and L is then identified by L11 >= 0, L22 >= 0, L12 = 0. Inputs are standardized with train-query mean/std (train only).
teacher.deviation_from_paper: Four declared cuts. (1) Single (sigma0, c) slice (0.20, 0.50) instead of the paper's 25-combination family, and the teacher does NOT take (sigma0, c) as inputs: the extrinsic-noise family dimension is cut, so nothing is claimed about generalization across (sigma0, c). (2) The paper's full joint temporally-decoupled W2 loss is approximated by a marginal-W2 + covariance-mismatch loss (per-dimension sorted-marginal squared W2 plus the Frobenius covariance mismatch at each observation time), because exact joint W2 in 2D has no closed form and a Sinkhorn solver is out of CPU scope; the approximation is declared and the H5 W2-loss clause is read with that bias. (3) The paper's torchsde-based training is replaced by plain Euler simulation at dt_sim = 0.01 with the same MLP sizes cut to [32, 32]. (4) Horizon extended from the printed [0, 1] to [0, 4] (see data generation). The RPA-DNA and NFkB examples, the experimental data, and the RNN/LSTM benchmarks are not treated today.
teacher.estimator: w2 (the distilled teacher, chosen A PRIORI because the paper's method is W2-based)

estimators_compared.em: vEM plain Euler-Maruyama Gaussian transition likelihood over dt_obs = 0.05: mean x + f*dt, covariance (L L^T)*dt with f and L frozen at the interval start
estimators_compared.w2: vW2 simulation-based estimator: teacher simulated from the common initial condition (0, 1) at dt_sim = 0.01; loss = mean over observation times of [sum over dimensions of the sorted-marginal squared W2 distance between simulated and train-trajectory states, plus 0.5 * ||Cov_sim - Cov_train||_F^2 at each observation time)
